messages.content: Phoenix is wrapped, and now I need a very different trip: Boise for Lena’s club volleyball weekend, Jan. 24 to 26. Three of us, driving from Salt Lake City after school Friday if roads behave. Tournament is in the Nampa area, and we may see relatives in Meridian on Sunday. Can you help me choose a hotel zone before I place a hold?
Yes. Before I rank the zones, do you know the first Saturday wave time yet, and are you trying for one room with two queens or two rooms?

Schedule isn’t posted. Team says games could start anywhere between 8 and 10 Saturday. One room with two queens. The team block is near the venue, but they only have a few 2Q rooms and breakfast is not included.

Then the zones stack up like this: Nampa/team hotel is best for the morning drive and team coordination, but weaker for breakfast and late-arrival food; Meridian adds about 18 to 25 minutes to the venue, but has easier Friday dinner, likely included breakfast, and is better for Sunday relatives; downtown Boise has the most food, but adds the most Saturday morning drive and usually more parking hassle. With the start time unknown, I’d hold Meridian if it is cancellable and only use the team hotel if they can guarantee two queens.
The Meridian one I’m seeing has breakfast, free parking, and a two-queen room. It’s not fancy but close to Eagle Road restaurants. Is that too far if we draw an early wave?

Not too far, but it needs an earlier alarm. For an 8:00 first match, assume team arrival or check-in around 7:15. From central Meridian to Nampa, I’d plan to leave the hotel around 6:40, earlier if roads are slick. If breakfast starts at 6:00, it works; if breakfast starts at 6:30, you’ll want a grab-and-go backup.
The road piece is what worries me. We probably can’t leave SLC until 3:45 or 4 on Friday. Is driving still sensible, or should I have a flight backup?

Driving is sensible if the forecast is normal winter, but 4:00 is the latest I’d call comfortable. SLC to Meridian is usually about five and a half hours before weather, gas, and dinner. A realistic arrival is 10:00 to 11:00 p.m.; blowing snow near Twin Falls can push that later. A flight backup is useful only if you are willing to decide 24 to 36 hours out, because three last-minute SLC-BOI seats plus a rental can get expensive fast.
I’d rather not buy backup flights now. If weather gets bad, maybe we leave earlier or stop in Twin Falls. What should I ask the hotels before I hold one?

Ask Meridian: exact cancellation deadline, whether late check-in after 11 is protected, breakfast start time Saturday and Sunday, whether they can do breakfast bags if you leave before it opens, any parking fee, and whether the two-queen room is guaranteed rather than just requested. Ask the team hotel the same, plus whether the block rate has a shorter cancellation window or first-night deposit.
If the team hotel has no breakfast but is five minutes from the venue, is that worth it?

Only if Saturday starts very early or Lena really needs to be with the team group. Otherwise the Meridian trade-off is cleaner: easier Friday dinner, breakfast handled, free parking, Sunday relatives nearby, and better cancellation flexibility. The five-minute hotel saves stress Saturday morning but gives some of it back Friday night and at breakfast.
Could we hold both for a week?

Yes, if both are fully cancellable and neither has a deposit. Put calendar holds for both cancellation deadlines. If one has a 48-hour deadline and the other releases earlier, use the tighter one as the decision date. I would not hold a nonrefundable team room while the tournament schedule is still unknown.
Okay, make me a practical action plan for today.

Today: place a cancellable hold on the Meridian two-queen room if it guarantees the bed setup, breakfast, and free parking; call the team hotel and ask whether any two-queen block rooms are cancellable until at least midweek before arrival; do not book flights now; set a weather check for Wednesday night and Friday morning; and plan a packed dinner or snack option so you can keep moving if I-84 is slow. If the Saturday wave comes out early, we can revisit whether the Nampa room is worth the breakfast trade-off.

messages.content: Boise update: schedule posted. Saturday check-in is 7:15 in Nampa, first match at 8. Sunday bracket could run until 2 or 3. We cannot leave SLC before 4:15 Friday, and the forecast has blowing snow around Twin Falls. Team block releases tonight; Meridian breakfast room is still cancellable. What would you book?

Book Meridian, unless the team hotel can guarantee two queens with a painless cancellation by tonight. The early start hurts, but breakfast, free parking, Friday food, and Sunday Meridian relatives all line up. I’d rather absorb a 25-minute Saturday drive than get stuck with no breakfast and a tighter hotel policy.
What time do we need to leave the hotel Saturday?
Aim to be out the door at 6:35. That gives 35 to 40 minutes for winter driving and parking, with cushion for the 7:15 check-in. If roads are icy, leave at 6:20 and let breakfast be grab-and-go.
Breakfast starts at 6:30, which is not ideal.

Then treat hotel breakfast as Sunday’s benefit, not Saturday’s solution. Call tonight and ask if they can set out coffee, fruit, yogurt, or breakfast bags by 6:00. Either way, pack bagels, protein bars, and water bottles before you leave Salt Lake.
Should I keep the downtown backup?

No. Cancel the downtown backup now if it has gone up and doesn’t improve the drive. Keep only Meridian, plus the team block for a few hours if it is refundable. If the team block charges tonight or has no guaranteed two-queen room, let it go.
And the Friday drive plan?

Leave SLC as close to 4:15 as possible with dinner already packed or picked up before you hit I-84. Check Idaho 511 before Snowville and again near Burley. If the Twin Falls stretch is under warning or visibility is poor, stop in Twin Falls and call Meridian so they do not mark the room as a no-show; you may still pay for Friday, but it protects Saturday. Otherwise plan on Meridian arrival around 10:45 to 11:30. Final move: book Meridian cancellable two queens, cancel downtown today, and release the team block unless it stays refundable after the schedule is confirmed.

messages.content: I’m opening the late-February Puget Sound trip. Monday Feb. 24 I have a 6 to 8 p.m. admitted-student reception in Tacoma, Tuesday Feb. 25 a Bellevue transfer fair from 11:30 to 1:30, then an alumni dinner in Seattle at 6:30. Wednesday Feb. 26 is a noon counselor lunch in Everett. Coming from SLC. I need the route order, flight window, rental car question, and hotel areas.
That one has enough geography that arrival reliability matters. Two quick clarifiers before I rank it: are you checking a bag or carrying materials, and are you willing to move hotels once?

Carry-on plus a small box of materials if I can ship the rest. No checked bag planned. One hotel move is fine. I’d rather not be tense about a Monday arrival, but I also don’t want an unnecessary night if Monday morning is safe.

Short answer: arrive Sunday afternoon. A Monday morning nonstop can work on paper, but it leaves too many ways for traffic, baggage or material pickup, and hotel logistics to stack up before a 6 p.m. Tacoma reception. I’d target SLC-SEA Sunday landing by 3:30 or 4:00, rent a car, stay Tacoma Sunday and Monday, move to Bellevue Tuesday, and fly home Wednesday after the Everett lunch on a 5 p.m. or later SEA-SLC nonstop.
What would Monday morning look like if I tried it anyway?

Best case, you land around 9:30 or 10:00, get the car, drive to Tacoma, drop bags or materials, and still have several hours before the reception. The risk is that a delay turns into a 1 p.m. arrival, then you are eating lunch in the car and hoping the hotel can help before check-in. I would avoid any Monday itinerary landing after noon. Sunday costs one extra hotel night, but it protects the event.
Could Paine Field help because of Everett on Wednesday, or is SEA still the right airport?

SEA is still the practical anchor. Paine Field would help only at the very end, and SLC-PAE options are usually much thinner and more likely to involve a connection. Since the first fixed event is Tacoma, SEA gives you better nonstop choice and easier car pickup. For Wednesday, Everett to SEA is manageable if you do not book the return too early.
For flights, include Delta if the nonstop schedule is comparable, but I’m open if Alaska times are cleaner.

Good search set: outbound Sunday SLC-SEA nonstops departing late morning to midafternoon and landing before 4; return Wednesday SEA-SLC nonstops from about 5:30 to 7:30. Compare Delta and Alaska on schedule first, fare second. I would not take a connection on this route unless nonstop pricing is wildly out of policy.
Do I really need a rental car? Parking in Seattle is never fun.

For this route, yes to a rental car, with one exception: use rideshare for the Tuesday Seattle dinner if parking looks annoying. Car versus rideshare: rental car gives control for Tacoma to Bellevue to Everett, helps with materials, and avoids relying on long suburban rides during commute windows; rideshare saves parking fees but could be expensive and unpredictable across four cities. The car is worth it, but check hotel parking costs before booking.
Hotel sequence: Tacoma Sunday and Monday, then Bellevue Tuesday? Or just Bellevue all three nights?

Tacoma Sunday/Monday plus Bellevue Tuesday is the best balance. Bellevue all three nights avoids a move, but you would drive back north late Monday after the reception and start the trip with more freeway time. Tacoma two nights lets you settle in Sunday, be close to Monday’s reception, then drive north Tuesday morning with plenty of time for the 11:30 fair. Moving Tuesday also shortens Wednesday to Everett.
My Tacoma reception is near University of Puget Sound. I need dinner to be easy Sunday night and probably after the Monday reception too.

Then look at downtown Tacoma, waterfront, or the Proctor-adjacent side if rates are reasonable. Downtown/waterfront gives better restaurants and a 10 to 15 minute drive to UPS, but verify parking fees. South Tacoma or Tacoma Mall can be cheaper with easier parking and breakfast, but it is less pleasant for a late dinner. I’d shortlist a breakfast-included downtown or near-downtown option first, then a Tacoma Mall backup if prices jump.
Breakfast included would help if it doesn’t force me too far out. Monday morning is prep time, not a sit-down brunch.

Then prioritize a reliable included breakfast over a full-service lobby restaurant for Tacoma. Look for a Holiday Inn Express, Hampton, or similar near downtown/Tacoma Dome if the location is still reasonable to UPS. If the best restaurant-heavy hotel lacks breakfast, it can still work, but only if there is a coffee shop within a short walk or drive and parking is clear.
For Tuesday, the transfer fair is at Bellevue College and the alumni dinner is on Capitol Hill.

That points to Eastgate/Factoria or southeast Bellevue for Tuesday night. You would be close to Bellevue College, parking is usually simpler than downtown Bellevue, and Capitol Hill is a reasonable rideshare from there in the evening. Downtown Bellevue is nicer for dinner choices but not necessary since your dinner is in Seattle. For Wednesday, Eastgate to Everett is longer than Lynnwood, but still workable if you leave around 10:15.
I don’t love luggage sitting in the car all Tuesday while I’m at the fair.

Build in a bag drop. Leave Tacoma around 9:00, reach the Bellevue-area hotel around 10:00, and ask for early bag storage even if the room is not ready. Then go to Bellevue College for the 11:30 fair. If the hotel cannot hold bags, keep the carry-on covered in the trunk and bring the materials inside with you, but I’d choose a hotel that confirms bag storage.
What return flight time is safe Wednesday?

If the Everett lunch is noon to about 1:15, do not book anything before 5. Everett to SEA can be 60 to 90 minutes with traffic, then you still need fuel, rental return, and security. A 5:30 departure is the earliest I’d call reasonable; 6:30 or 7 gives you real breathing room if the lunch runs long.
Can you wrap this into the plan I should price first?

Price this first: SLC-SEA Sunday Feb. 23 nonstop landing by 3:30 or 4, with Delta and Alaska both in the search; rental car from SEA, returning Wednesday; Tacoma hotel Sunday and Monday near downtown, waterfront, or a reasonable UPS drive, with included breakfast, clear parking cost, late check-in, and nearby dinner verified; Tuesday hotel in Eastgate/Factoria or southeast Bellevue with breakfast, parking, and confirmed early bag storage; rideshare from the Bellevue hotel to Capitol Hill dinner if parking looks difficult; Wednesday counselor lunch in Everett, then drive to SEA and book SEA-SLC no earlier than 5:30, preferably closer to 6:30 if the fare is comparable. Main uncertainties to verify are hotel parking fees, breakfast start times, bag storage Tuesday, and whether the Tacoma venue has easy event parking.
